blockers.quote: Untrained, people tell a lie from the truth about 54% of the time (c06). Everyone else is a coin flip that wants to believe you.
blockers.why: Row c06 establishes that untrained judges average 54% accuracy (barely above a 50% coin flip) and exhibit a truth bias by judging 61% of truths as nondeceptive and 47% of lies as deceptive. The line overstates and distorts the finding by separating untrained people from a supposed 'everyone else' who are a coin flip, and by attributing an active intent ('wants to believe you') to an aggregate truth-bias baseline.
blockers.fix: Untrained, people tell a lie from the truth about 54% of the time (c06)—barely above a coin flip, leaning toward believing.
